newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan told U.S. c/a surplus not expanding - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan told U.S. c/a surplus not expanding - MOF.

text.p: Japan has told the United States its current account surplus is still on a declining trend, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Monday.
Mitsuzuka said he made the remark to U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin at a bilateral meeting held on the sidelines of the weekend meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations.
Mitsuzuka was speaking at a parliamentary committee meeting.
Asked what he told Rubin during the bilateral talks, the finance minister said: "I told him that I did not think the current account balance was worsening as is viewed in the United States."

Yoshio Suzuki, a Lower House member with the key opposition New Frontier Party (Shinshinto) who was questioning Mitsuzuka, pointed out that current account balance in real terms stood at 1.6 trillion yen in January to March period last year, which expanded to an average two trillion yen in the July to September period.
The Finance Ministry announced earlier on Monday that the current account surplus in nominal terms for 1996 shrank 30.9 percent from a year earlier to 7.1806 trillion yen.
